topic: Declaration of Commerciality and FLNG development concept (2025-2026)
wiki_text: On 14 November 2025, PETRONAS and Suriname's state oil company Staatsolie declared commerciality (DoC) for the Sloanea gas field in offshore Block 52, described as Suriname's first gas development milestone. PETRONAS holds an 80% participating interest in the block and is operator; Paradise Oil Company (POC), a Staatsolie subsidiary, holds the remaining 20%. The selected development concept comprises gas production wells, subsea infrastructure, and a newbuild floating LNG (FLNG) facility — billed as the region's first — situated roughly 120 km offshore at about 450 m water depth. Wison New Energies was awarded the detailed feasibility study (DFS) for the FLNG unit in 2025. A final investment decision is targeted for the second half of 2026, with first gas expected in 2030. ExxonMobil Exploration & Production Suriname, formerly a Block 52 partner, exited the block in late 2024, leaving PETRONAS as operator and majority holder.

Through 2024-2025, multiple Surinamese and Dutch outlets reported that the Firebird LNG / Port of Nickerie project had seen little concrete progress since 2023. Key participants withdrew: the Port of Rotterdam Authority declined to participate after submitting an action plan, and dredging contractor Van Oord also stepped back, per local reporting. Articles such as 'Port of Nickerie struggling to get off the ground: delays and doubts about realization' questioned whether the terminal would be built, though the director of port operator NV Havenbeheer maintained in 2025 that the project was still advancing. Sponsors Phoenix Development Holding Co (Houston) and MAD Energy (Idaho) had previously described the ~2.7 mtpa project as fully funded through FID, with operations 28 months after a final investment decision. No FID had been taken as of mid-2025.
